Unfortunately, It is complicated to resolve with a regular adblock rule because the website is being protected by service of Ad-Shield that is an anti-adblock company.

## Userscript Installation
Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

Unfortunately, It is complicated to resolve with a regular adblock rule because the website is being protected by service of Ad-Shield that is an anti-adblock company.

## Userscript Installation
Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

issue.title: www.youtube.com

labels.name: T: Incorrect Blocking
labels.description: Website or app not working properly due to filtering

labels.name: A: Cannot reproduce
labels.description: Filters devs cannot reproduce this issue

issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS. 


Previous issue https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/198973

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Social Widget) [https://fp3-siken.com/kakomon.php](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffp3-siken.com%2Fkakomon.php) ### Comment > > > Bug Report: Social share buttons are no longer blocked > > Description > > On the target website (reported in this issue), the social media share buttons are no longer blocked and remain visible. > > Conditions for Reproduction > > This issue occurs only when both of the following filters are added and enabled as Custom Filters (rather than enabling them from the app’s default filter list): > > • Japanese Filter (Full / Unoptimized): https://filters.adtidy.org/ios/filters/7.txt > • Social Media Filter (Full / Unoptimized): https://filters.adtidy.org/ios/filters/4.txt > > Notes on when the issue does NOT occur: > > • Adding other filters as custom filters does not trigger the issue. > • Default Social Media Filter + Custom Japanese Filter -> Works as expected. > • Custom Social Media Filter + Default Japanese Filter -> Works as expected. > • The issue strictly occurs when both are registered as custom filters. > > Screenshots / Guide to the Reproduction Page > > I have attached screenshots that show, step by step, how to navigate from the site’s top page to the page where the issue can be reproduced. Please refer to them to reach the affected page and confirm that the share buttons remain visible. > > Workaround > > Adding a user rule to hide the specific element temporarily resolves the issue. > Interestingly, adding the exact rule that should already be included in the Social Media Filter as a user rule also fixes it. This indicates that the rule itself works fine, but something within the filter combination is overriding or negating it. > > Possible Cause > > I suspect that a rule present in the full (unoptimized) version but removed in the optimized (built-in) version of one of these filters is interfering with the hiding of the share buttons. > Since adding filters with even more rules than the Japanese Filter (e.g., the Cookie Notices filter) does not reproduce the issue, I have concluded this is not caused by hitting the iOS Content Blocker rule limit. > > Why using “Optimized Filters” is not a solution > > I browse a massive number of websites for both work and personal use. Reporting broken sites caused by rules stripped during optimization defeats the purpose. As long as I am within the iOS rule limit, using full versions via custom filters should fundamentally work. > > Request > > Please investigate and fix the cause, or explain the root cause of this conflict. > I am happy to provide logs, screenshots, exported settings, or specific related rules if needed. The attached screenshots should make the reproduction steps clear, but please let me know before closing this as “Cannot reproduce”—I am fully willing to assist in confirming the reproduction steps. > > Additionally, the operator of this website runs several other websites using the exact same layout (listed below). It would be greatly appreciated if these could be addressed as well. If I need to create separate issues for them, please let me know. > > Thanks. > ### Screenshots

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Social Widget) [https://fp3-siken.com/kakomon.php](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffp3-siken.com%2Fkakomon.php) ### Comment > > > Bug Report: Social share buttons are no longer blocked > > Description > > On the target website (reported in this issue), the social media share buttons are no longer blocked and remain visible. > > Conditions for Reproduction > > This issue occurs only when both of the following filters are added and enabled as Custom Filters (rather than enabling them from the app’s default filter list): > > • Japanese Filter (Full / Unoptimized): https://filters.adtidy.org/ios/filters/7.txt > • Social Media Filter (Full / Unoptimized): https://filters.adtidy.org/ios/filters/4.txt > > Notes on when the issue does NOT occur: > > • Adding other filters as custom filters does not trigger the issue. > • Default Social Media Filter + Custom Japanese Filter -> Works as expected. > • Custom Social Media Filter + Default Japanese Filter -> Works as expected. > • The issue strictly occurs when both are registered as custom filters. > > Screenshots / Guide to the Reproduction Page > > I have attached screenshots that show, step by step, how to navigate from the site’s top page to the page where the issue can be reproduced. Please refer to them to reach the affected page and confirm that the share buttons remain visible. > > Workaround > > Adding a user rule to hide the specific element temporarily resolves the issue. > Interestingly, adding the exact rule that should already be included in the Social Media Filter as a user rule also fixes it. This indicates that the rule itself works fine, but something within the filter combination is overriding or negating it. > > Possible Cause > > I suspect that a rule present in the full (unoptimized) version but removed in the optimized (built-in) version of one of these filters is interfering with the hiding of the share buttons. > Since adding filters with even more rules than the Japanese Filter (e.g., the Cookie Notices filter) does not reproduce the issue, I have concluded this is not caused by hitting the iOS Content Blocker rule limit. > > Why using “Optimized Filters” is not a solution > > I browse a massive number of websites for both work and personal use. Reporting broken sites caused by rules stripped during optimization defeats the purpose. As long as I am within the iOS rule limit, using full versions via custom filters should fundamentally work. > > Request > > Please investigate and fix the cause, or explain the root cause of this conflict. > I am happy to provide logs, screenshots, exported settings, or specific related rules if needed. The attached screenshots should make the reproduction steps clear, but please let me know before closing this as “Cannot reproduce”—I am fully willing to assist in confirming the reproduction steps. > > Additionally, the operator of this website runs several other websites using the exact same layout (listed below). It would be greatly appreciated if these could be addressed as well. If I need to create separate issues for them, please let me know. > > Thanks. > ### Screenshots

Unfortunately, It is complicated to resolve with a regular adblock rule because the website is being protected by service of Ad-Shield that is an anti-adblock company.

## Userscript Installation
Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

# Sorry. The website is infected by AdShield, Inc.

Unfortunately, It is complicated to resolve with a regular adblock rule because the website is being protected by service of Ad-Shield that is an anti-adblock company.

## Userscript Installation
Please block Ad-Shield advertisement by installing [tinyShield userscript](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield).
Please check its installation guideline written in English by visiting [this URL](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.md).

If you can understand Korean language, please refer https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/blob/main/README.ko.md.

New change of tinyShield's build script for Apple Safari Extension user (made at 2026 Apr 21) is available.

## Still Have a Problem?
An issue is occurred when the userscript is applied, please report to [this issue tracker](https://github.com/FilteringDev/tinyShield/issues).

issue.title: intercelestial.com
issue.body: ### What happens https://intercelestial.com/ still shows the "Your network is blocking ads" wall in Safari with content-blocker filters (AdGuard Base, Safari build v2.4.96.6). I'm the developer of wBlock, which compiles your Safari filter builds with SafariConverterLib, so this should also hit AdGuard for Safari and iOS. The wall comes from "AntiAdBlock Core". The site serves its loader from a random first-party path, so domain rules never see it: - `https://intercelestial.com/66687a7a3b/app.77c7f7d98662c25e.js` (today) - `https://intercelestial.com/a36492a4b6/...` (two days ago) - `intercelestial.com/b87d50d081/bundle.480ced44dbae0a92.js` (from BlazDT in #243080) ### Suggested rule ``` ! https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/243613 !#if (adguard_app_ios || adguard_ext_safari) /^https:\/\/intercelestial\.com\/[0-9a-f]+\/[a-z]+\.[0-9a-f]+\.js/$script,domain=intercelestial.com !#endif ``` The current rules lean on `redirect-rule=nooptext`, which Safari content blockers can't do. So the loader's fetches to five ad hosts fail and it shows the wall. Blocking the loader itself avoids all of that. Safari doesn't accept `{n,m}` in regex rules, so the pattern uses `+`. It only matches a hex folder plus `name.hash.js`. I tested it in Safari 27 on macOS. Without the rule the wall shows every time. With it Safari blocks the loader and the page loads normally. issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
[https://mused.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmused.com%2F)

### Comment
> **AdGuard DNS Family Protection blocks mused.com and mused.org as adult content, but both are educational sites.**
> 
> `dig @94.140.14.15 mused.com` (and www.mused.com, iiif.mused.com, static.mused.com, civs.mused.com, mused.org) returns the family block address 94.140.14.35. The Default server does not block them.
> 
> The label appears to date from earlier owners of mused.com, who ran an adult age-gated site (2003-2005) and an NSFW video blog (2014-2015) on the domain:
> - https://web.archive.org/web/20030607210848/http://mused.com/
> - https://web.archive.org/web/20140402040244/http://mused.com/category/nsfw/
> 
> The domain changed owners before 2022. mused.com is now Mused, an educational platform of 3D tours of archaeological sites and museum collections, used by K-12 schools and universities (school library: https://mused.com/edu/). mused.org is its sister site for the same tours. Some collection items are classical artworks shown in their museum context; there is no adult content. Cisco Talos categorizes the domains as Education and Museums.
> 
> Please remove mused.com and mused.org (including subdomains) from the adult category.

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
[https://mused.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmused.com%2F)

### Comment
> **AdGuard DNS Family Protection blocks mused.com and mused.org as adult content, but both are educational sites.**
> 
> `dig @94.140.14.15 mused.com` (and www.mused.com, iiif.mused.com, static.mused.com, civs.mused.com, mused.org) returns the family block address 94.140.14.35. The Default server does not block them.
> 
> The label appears to date from earlier owners of mused.com, who ran an adult age-gated site (2003-2005) and an NSFW video blog (2014-2015) on the domain:
> - https://web.archive.org/web/20030607210848/http://mused.com/
> - https://web.archive.org/web/20140402040244/http://mused.com/category/nsfw/
> 
> The domain changed owners before 2022. mused.com is now Mused, an educational platform of 3D tours of archaeological sites and museum collections, used by K-12 schools and universities (school library: https://mused.com/edu/). mused.org is its sister site for the same tours. Some collection items are classical artworks shown in their museum context; there is no adult content. Cisco Talos categorizes the domains as Education and Museums.
> 
> Please remove mused.com and mused.org (including subdomains) from the adult category.

### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
[https://mused.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmused.com%2F)

### Comment
> **AdGuard DNS Family Protection blocks mused.com and mused.org as adult content, but both are educational sites.**
> 
> `dig @94.140.14.15 mused.com` (and www.mused.com, iiif.mused.com, static.mused.com, civs.mused.com, mused.org) returns the family block address 94.140.14.35. The Default server does not block them.
> 
> The label appears to date from earlier owners of mused.com, who ran an adult age-gated site (2003-2005) and an NSFW video blog (2014-2015) on the domain:
> - https://web.archive.org/web/20030607210848/http://mused.com/
> - https://web.archive.org/web/20140402040244/http://mused.com/category/nsfw/
> 
> The domain changed owners before 2022. mused.com is now Mused, an educational platform of 3D tours of archaeological sites and museum collections, used by K-12 schools and universities (school library: https://mused.com/edu/). mused.org is its sister site for the same tours. Some collection items are classical artworks shown in their museum context; there is no adult content. Cisco Talos categorizes the domains as Education and Museums.
> 
> Please remove mused.com and mused.org (including subdomains) from the adult category.

I'm the developer of wBlock, which compiles your Safari filter builds with SafariConverterLib, so this should also hit AdGuard for Safari and iOS. The wall comes from "AntiAdBlock Core". The site serves its loader from a random first-party path, so domain rules never see it: - `https://intercelestial.com/66687a7a3b/app.77c7f7d98662c25e.js` (today) - `https://intercelestial.com/a36492a4b6/...` (two days ago) - `intercelestial.com/b87d50d081/bundle.480ced44dbae0a92.js` (from BlazDT in #243080) ### Suggested rule ``` ! https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/243613 !#if (adguard_app_ios || adguard_ext_safari) /^https:\/\/intercelestial\.com\/[0-9a-f]+\/[a-z]+\.[0-9a-f]+\.js/$script,domain=intercelestial.com !#endif ``` The current rules lean on `redirect-rule=nooptext`, which Safari content blockers can't do. So the loader's fetches to five ad hosts fail and it shows the wall. Blocking the loader itself avoids all of that. Safari doesn't accept `{n,m}` in regex rules, so the pattern uses `+`. It only matches a hex folder plus `name.hash.js`. I tested it in Safari 27 on macOS. Without the rule the wall shows every time. With it Safari blocks the loader and the page loads normally. ### Issue URL (Incorrect Blocking)
[https://mused.com/](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmused.com%2F)

### Comment
> **AdGuard DNS Family Protection blocks mused.com and mused.org as adult content, but both are educational sites.**
> 
> `dig @94.140.14.15 mused.com` (and www.mused.com, iiif.mused.com, static.mused.com, civs.mused.com, mused.org) returns the family block address 94.140.14.35. The Default server does not block them.
> 
> The label appears to date from earlier owners of mused.com, who ran an adult age-gated site (2003-2005) and an NSFW video blog (2014-2015) on the domain:
> - https://web.archive.org/web/20030607210848/http://mused.com/
> - https://web.archive.org/web/20140402040244/http://mused.com/category/nsfw/
> 
> The domain changed owners before 2022. mused.com is now Mused, an educational platform of 3D tours of archaeological sites and museum collections, used by K-12 schools and universities (school library: https://mused.com/edu/). mused.org is its sister site for the same tours. Some collection items are classical artworks shown in their museum context; there is no adult content. Cisco Talos categorizes the domains as Education and Museums.
> 
> Please remove mused.com and mused.org (including subdomains) from the adult category.

issue.body: ### What happens https://intercelestial.com/ still shows the "Your network is blocking ads" wall in Safari with content-blocker filters (AdGuard Base, Safari build v2.4.96.6). I'm the developer of wBlock, which compiles your Safari filter builds with SafariConverterLib, so this should also hit AdGuard for Safari and iOS. The wall comes from "AntiAdBlock Core". The site serves its loader from a random first-party path, so domain rules never see it: - `https://intercelestial.com/66687a7a3b/app.77c7f7d98662c25e.js` (today) - `https://intercelestial.com/a36492a4b6/...` (two days ago) - `intercelestial.com/b87d50d081/bundle.480ced44dbae0a92.js` (from BlazDT in #243080) ### Suggested rule ``` ! https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/243613 !#if (adguard_app_ios || adguard_ext_safari) /^https:\/\/intercelestial\.com\/[0-9a-f]+\/[a-z]+\.[0-9a-f]+\.js/$script,domain=intercelestial.com !#endif ``` The current rules lean on `redirect-rule=nooptext`, which Safari content blockers can't do. So the loader's fetches to five ad hosts fail and it shows the wall. Blocking the loader itself avoids all of that. Safari doesn't accept `{n,m}` in regex rules, so the pattern uses `+`. It only matches a hex folder plus `name.hash.js`. I tested it in Safari 27 on macOS. Without the rule the wall shows every time. With it Safari blocks the loader and the page loads normally. Screenshots below. ### Screenshots Without the rule: With the rule:

issue.body: ### What happens https://intercelestial.com/ still shows the "Your network is blocking ads" wall in Safari with content-blocker filters (AdGuard Base, Safari build v2.4.96.6). I'm the developer of wBlock, which compiles your Safari filter builds with SafariConverterLib, so this should also hit AdGuard for Safari and iOS. The wall comes from "AntiAdBlock Core". The site serves its loader from a random first-party path, so domain rules never see it: - `https://intercelestial.com/66687a7a3b/app.77c7f7d98662c25e.js` (today) - `https://intercelestial.com/a36492a4b6/...` (two days ago) - `intercelestial.com/b87d50d081/bundle.480ced44dbae0a92.js` (from BlazDT in #243080) ### Suggested rule ``` ! https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/243613 !#if (adguard_app_ios || adguard_ext_safari) /^https:\/\/intercelestial\.com\/[0-9a-f]+\/[a-z]+\.[0-9a-f]+\.js/$script,domain=intercelestial.com !#endif ``` The current rules lean on `redirect-rule=nooptext`, which Safari content blockers can't do. So the loader's fetches to five ad hosts fail and it shows the wall. Blocking the loader itself avoids all of that. Safari doesn't accept `{n,m}` in regex rules, so the pattern uses `+`. It only matches a hex folder plus `name.hash.js`. I tested it in Safari 27 on macOS. Without the rule the wall shows every time. With it Safari blocks the loader and the page loads normally. Screenshots below. ### Screenshots Without the rule: With the rule:

issue.body: ### What happens https://intercelestial.com/ still shows the "Your network is blocking ads" wall in Safari with content-blocker filters (AdGuard Base, Safari build v2.4.96.6). I'm the developer of wBlock, which compiles your Safari filter builds with SafariConverterLib, so this should also hit AdGuard for Safari and iOS. The wall comes from "AntiAdBlock Core". The site serves its loader from a random first-party path, so domain rules never see it: - `https://intercelestial.com/66687a7a3b/app.77c7f7d98662c25e.js` (today) - `https://intercelestial.com/a36492a4b6/...` (two days ago) - `intercelestial.com/b87d50d081/bundle.480ced44dbae0a92.js` (from BlazDT in #243080) ### Suggested rule ``` ! https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/243613 !#if (adguard_app_ios || adguard_ext_safari) /^https:\/\/intercelestial\.com\/[0-9a-f]+\/[a-z]+\.[0-9a-f]+\.js/$script,domain=intercelestial.com !#endif ``` The current rules lean on `redirect-rule=nooptext`, which Safari content blockers can't do. So the loader's fetches to five ad hosts fail and it shows the wall. Blocking the loader itself avoids all of that. Safari doesn't accept `{n,m}` in regex rules, so the pattern uses `+`. It only matches a hex folder plus `name.hash.js`. I tested it in Safari 27 on macOS. Without the rule the wall shows every time. With it Safari blocks the loader and the page loads normally. Screenshots below. ### Screenshots Without the rule: With the rule:

@ghajini

Sorry for the confusion and trouble.
It can be reproduced after changing the region/language to United States / English at [https://www.dji.com/mobile/choose-your-language](https://www.dji.com/mobile/choose-your-language).
It turns out it wasn't an iPad-specific issue, but a region/language difference:
The US/English site serves a different banner template (.download-app-container instead of .universal-product-tip), and the close button is .download-icon-close. Because of this, the current rule(` www.dji.com#%#//scriptlet('trusted-click-element', '.universal-product-tip a.universal-product-tip-link[href^="https://cdp-vg.djiservice.org/"] ~ .close-icon')`) doesn't match the elements.

Could you please check it once more with the US/English setting when you have time? Really appreciate your help!

issue.body: ### What happens https://intercelestial.com/ still shows the "Your network is blocking ads" wall in Safari with content-blocker filters (AdGuard Base, Safari build v2.4.96.6). I'm the developer of wBlock, which compiles your Safari filter builds with SafariConverterLib, so this should also hit AdGuard for Safari and iOS. The wall comes from "AntiAdBlock Core". The site serves its loader from a random first-party path, so domain rules never see it: - `https://intercelestial.com/66687a7a3b/app.77c7f7d98662c25e.js` (today) - `https://intercelestial.com/a36492a4b6/...` (two days ago) - `intercelestial.com/b87d50d081/bundle.480ced44dbae0a92.js` (from BlazDT in #243080) ### Suggested rule ``` ! https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/243613 !#if (adguard_app_ios || adguard_ext_safari) /^https:\/\/intercelestial\.com\/[0-9a-f]+\/[a-z]+\.[0-9a-f]+\.js/$script,domain=intercelestial.com !#endif ``` The current rules lean on `redirect-rule=nooptext`, which Safari content blockers can't do. So the loader's fetches to five ad hosts fail and it shows the wall. Blocking the loader itself avoids all of that. Safari doesn't accept `{n,m}` in regex rules, so the pattern uses `+`. It only matches a hex folder plus `name.hash.js`. I tested it in Safari 27 on macOS. Without the rule the wall shows every time. With it Safari blocks the loader and the page loads normally. ### Comment
> **AdGuard DNS Family Protection blocks mused.com and mused.org as adult content, but both are educational sites.**

> 
> The label appears to date from earlier owners of mused.com, who ran an adult age-gated site (2003-2005) and an NSFW video blog (2014-2015) on the domain:
> - https://web.archive.org/web/20030607210848/http://mused.com/
> - https://web.archive.org/web/20140402040244/http://mused.com/category/nsfw/
> 
> The domain changed owners before 2022. mused.com is now Mused, an educational platform of 3D tours of archaeological sites and museum collections, used by K-12 schools and universities (school library: https://mused.com/edu/). mused.org is its sister site for the same tours. Some collection items are classical artworks shown in their museum context; there is no adult content. Cisco Talos categorizes the domains as Education and Museums.

issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS. 


Previous issue https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/198973
